chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjaj, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
We mentioned the partial eclipse of the moon and what people endure of its intensity. He said, then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When a part of it is revealed, it has been revealed.'
From him, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from 'Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Wasiti, who said:
I wrote to al-Rida (peace be upon him): When the sun and moon are eclipsed and I am riding and cannot dismount, he wrote to me: 'Pray on your mount upon which you are.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (Imam Musa ibn Ja'far, peace be upon him)
key_terms.انْجَلَى: Revealed/Cleared (referring to the celestial body emerging from shadow)
key_terms.انْكِسَاف: Partial eclipse (of the sun or moon)

ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer during an eclipse if they are riding and cannot get off their animal?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the criterion for the conclusion of the eclipse prayer, noting that the event is considered ended once any part of the celestial body becomes visible, while Imam al-Rida (AS) further clarifies the flexibility of performing this prayer while riding if dismounting is difficult. These rulings highlight the practical ease (rukhas) granted in Shia jurisprudence for celestial phenomena, linking the physical act of worship to the observable signs of Allah's power in the cosmos.
